local_articles.title: US Open women's singles: Three talking points
local_articles.snippet: Second-ranked Elena Rybakina has been inching toward the top spot for weeks and will get there if she reaches the semi-finals, but the Kazakh's prospects are clouded by injury concerns. Americans Coco Gauff or Jessica Pegula could also pounce if either bag the title and Sabalenka and Rybakina both falter in Flushing Meadows. Those closest in pursuit aren't the only players Sabalenka has to worry about as she tries to become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2012-2014 to win three straight US Open titles. Six-time Grand Slam winner Iga Swiatek thrust herself into the conversation with her first title of the season in Toronto, while Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala boosted her hard court credentials with a first career WTA title in Washington this month. questions.title: Which company will Liverpool announce as its main shirt sponsor for the 2027–28 season?
questions.background: Standard Chartered has been Liverpool's main shirt sponsor since 2010. This sponsorship gives the company prominent branding on the front of the club's playing shirts.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Liverpool FC's official announcement identifying the company with an agreed main front-of-shirt sponsorship deal covering the 2027–28 season. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the club announces the agreement, provided the announcement occurs between June 1 and December 31, 2026. The agreement's announcement, rather than the sponsorship's commencement, determines resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the sponsoring company. Sleeve sponsors, kit manufacturers, and other commercial partners do not qualify.

Latty flagged a recent 'big leadership change' at sleeve sponsor Expedia, lowering its odds of upgrading to front-of-shirt; replacing Expedia in the top 5 with Amazon (0.04) following the Aug 14 announcement that 1892 Holdings (including Jeff Bezos via K5 Sports, Amit Bhatia, Lakshmi Mittal's trust, and Eduardo Saverin) acquired a 38% stake in Liverpool (calibrated modestly given Borson's view that Bezos is a passive investor). AXA (0.07), Riyadh Air (0.05), and Qatar Airways (0.04) round out the top 5, leaving 60% on the wide global corporate field.
